message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo was one of the bloodiest engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  While exact figures differ slightly among contemporary reports and modern historians, the generally accepted totals are:

| Side | Killed & Wounded | Captured / Missing | Total Casualties |
|------|------------------|--------------------|------------------|
| **French** | ≈ 25 000 | ≈ 5 000 | ≈ 30 000 |
| **Allied (British‑Dutch‑German‑Belgian)** | ≈ 20 000 | ≈ 2 000 | ≈ 22 000 |

So, in aggregate, the battle produced roughly **47 000–50 000 casualties** (killed, wounded, missing or captured).  These numbers are rounded estimates; some sources quote slightly higher or lower figures depending on how they count wounded versus missing and whether they include later deaths from wounds.
